discussion_comments.comment_body: Addressed in `448d7f11e` — *fix(vcs): reject worktree clone with destination inside source and strip nested .git*. Please take another look.
Fixed in a5422b406b: a relative pointer is resolved against the SOURCE directory it was written in, not the copy. `remove_nested_git_files_strips_a_relative_pointer_into_this_repository` covers it.
Addressed in `448d7f11e` — *fix(vcs): reject worktree clone with destination inside source and strip nested .git*. Please take another look.

Fixed in 0f540de539: the bind-mount check compares the directory the destination would be created in with the SOURCE ITSELF by filesystem identity, not with the source's ancestors — a sibling in a shared parent is no longer refused. `destination_inside_source_accepts_a_sibling_in_a_shared_parent` covers it.
Fixed in c709e8ea3a: the cleanup skips the root `.git`; only nested entries are stripped. `remove_nested_git_files_strips_only_pointers_into_this_repository` asserts it.

Still open. `destination_aliases_source()` compares the directory the destination would be created in with the source by filesystem identity; when the destination sits under an existing directory below a bind alias, that directory is neither the source nor one of its ancestors, so the comparison misses it. Walking the existing directory's ancestors would close it — not done in this round, so the thread stays open.

Still open. `detach_repository()` copies `HEAD` and `index` but not the `sharedindex.*` sibling, so a split-index repository is detached with an index whose link extension points at a missing file and `git status` fails there — not done in this round, so the thread stays open.

Fixed in 70afaaaa60 (the refusal) and 1fb7f6da80 (its base): the routing is right, but the probe was the wrong gate for the refusal.

The probe asked whether the destination's filesystem can reflink a FILE. The recursion it was meant to prevent is not in the file copy: `linux_reflink::clone_tree` (crates/pi-iso/src/linux_reflink.rs:100-113) creates the destination inside the source FIRST and only then walks the source, and `copy_dir_contents` (crates/pi-iso/src/tree.rs) recurses on DIRECTORIES — so the walk finds the directory the copy just created and descends into it again until the path is too long. No file is cloned on that path, so the FICLONE syscall is never reached and the probe cannot predict the recursion.

So the probe made the refusal fire only where it was not needed and let the copy start exactly where it was fatal: it answered "no clone here" on a filesystem without FICLONE, the refusal was skipped, and the host-level candidate list still drove the copy — which recursed into the source until the path overflowed, and the plain checkout then took over after the copy had already mangled the tree. That is the failure issue #16076 reports, and it is filesystem-independent: the same walk recurses on btrfs too, where the files clone fine. Measured on this branch before the fix: 3 tests failed with `nested-dest/nested-dest/nested-dest/...` (ENAMETOOLONG) — `worktree_add_rejects_an_in_tree_destination_before_creating_the_branch`, `clone_first_worktree_rejects_destination_inside_source_behind_a_missing_component` and `clone_first_worktree_rejects_destination_behind_a_symlinked_parent`.

The refusal now applies wherever a copy would start: the destination is refused when it lands inside the source, on every filesystem, and the probe is gone because it had no remaining consumer. The refusal stays inside the existing gates, so a host with no cloning backend at all, and a repository whose own clone preconditions fail (sparse checkout, split index, a missing index), still check the destination out in place.

A destination OUTSIDE the source is unaffected and keeps the fallback this finding asked for: the copy lands in a fresh directory that never re-enters the source, so where the filesystem cannot copy, the attempt is cleaned up and the plain checkout takes over. That is now pinned by a new test, `a_destination_outside_the_source_still_falls_back_to_a_plain_checkout`, which asserts the caller gets a usable worktree and the reason is reported.

`cargo nextest run -p pi-vcs`: 119 passed, 0 failed. Reverting only the production guard (back to the probed one on this branch) turns 5 tests red, including the one above.

Answered at the current head `70afaaaa60` — the probe this finding asks for is gone, and the precheck no longer depends on the filesystem at all.

`clone_supported_on()` and the host-level `pi_iso::clone_candidates()` check are **deleted** (`crates/pi-vcs/src/git/mutate.rs` — no occurrence remains), and the in-tree refusal is now unconditional: `destination_inside_source(path, &source_root)` (`crates/pi-vcs/src/git/mutate.rs:653`) refuses the destination wherever a copy would start, on every filesystem, before any backend runs.

The reason is that the probe measured the wrong thing. `linux_reflink::clone_tree` (`crates/pi-iso/src/linux_reflink.rs:100-113`) creates the destination **inside** the source first and only then walks the source, and `copy_dir_contents` recurses on **directories** — so the walk finds the directory the copy just made and descends into it again until the path overflows. No file is cloned on that path, so the `FICLONE` syscall is never reached and no filesystem probe can predict the recursion; it is filesystem-independent (on btrfs the files clone fine and the walk recurses anyway — exactly what issue #16076 reports). Gating the refusal on "the filesystem can clone a FILE" therefore let the copy start exactly where it was fatal: "no clone here" on a filesystem without `FICLONE` skipped the refusal, the host-level candidate list still drove the copy, the recursion overflowed the path, and the plain checkout took over only after the copy had already mangled the tree.

`an_in_tree_destination_is_refused_whatever_the_filesystem_supports` (`crates/pi-vcs/src/git/mutate.rs:4622`) and `clone_first_worktree_rejects_destination_inside_source` (:3713) pin the refusal. What this finding correctly asks for — a destination **outside** the source is still copied, and where the filesystem cannot copy, the attempt is cleaned up and the plain checkout takes over — survives and is pinned by `a_destination_outside_the_source_still_falls_back_to_a_plain_checkout` (:4592). The refusal also stays inside the existing gates, so a host with no cloning backend, and a repo whose clone preconditions fail (sparseCheckout / splitIndex / missing index), still check out **in place**.

At the current head the crate suite is green (the branch owner's `cargo nextest run -p pi-vcs`: 119 passed, 0 failed; `cargo clippy -p pi-vcs --all-targets` and `rustfmt --check` clean), and RED on revert against the probed pre-fix source: 118 tests run, 5 failed — the 3 pre-existing recursion failures plus `clone_first_worktree_rejects_destination_inside_source` and `an_in_tree_destination_is_refused_whatever_the_filesystem_supports`, each with the growing `nested-dest/nested-dest/...` path.

Fixed in 19423f409dd3: `parse_core_worktree`'s section-header check required the line's trimmed final character to be `]`, so `[core] # note` and `[core]; note` (both valid git syntax — a comment after the header's closing bracket on the same line) left `in_core` false and `core.worktree` was ignored, falling back to the common metadata directory exactly as described. The header check now splits on the first `]` and accepts an empty, `#`-led, or `;`-led trailer after it. Added `core_worktree_recognizes_section_header_with_trailing_hash_comment` and `_semicolon_comment` regression tests (`cargo nextest run -p pi-vcs core_worktree` now covers 5 cases, all passing).

Fixed in 36483ac0eccc. When a line ends in a backslash, `decode_config_value` now takes the next line from the caller's line iterator and keeps decoding with the same quote state, so `worktree = /path/ma\` followed by `in` decodes to `/path/main`, as `git config --get core.worktree` returns for that text. The continuation line is consumed and not parsed again as its own line. Added `core_worktree_joins_backslash_continued_lines` for the unquoted and quoted forms; it failed before the change with `/path/ma`.
